Osric Dunn.narrative: I am headman of Thornby, and the weight of forty baskets of grain sits on me every time I load fish for Brackenford. The sea has been good to us but not good enough to pay that ledger and keep the village fed. My brother drowned below Edda's light, and I will not pretend otherwise. Perrin is a good lad and will do as he likes about Inga; I have heard the talk and I wave it off.
goals: pay down the grain debt without starving Thornby
see Edda Wray answer for my brother's boat
keep Perrin and Inga's courtship from becoming village business
get the marks Aldwyn Bexley owes me
learn to read the tide-race past the cape well enough to fish it safely
see Perrin settled with a boat and a hearth of his own

relations.name: Rona Dunn
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the fire and the tally in her head; I would be lost without her.

relations.name: Perrin Dunn
relations.label: son
relations.note: A good fisherman, and he will do as he likes about Inga.

relations.name: Inga Dunn
relations.label: niece
relations.note: Fond of her; she works hard at the nets and the smoke shed.

relations.name: Hob Dunn
relations.label: ward
relations.note: A quiet lad; he earns his bread mending nets.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: The ledger is his, and he will not forget a basket.

relations.name: Edda Wray
relations.label: accused
relations.note: My brother's boat went on the rocks below her light; she lit it wrong and Thornby knows it.

relations.name: Rook Tarn
relations.label: tally-keeper
relations.note: He keeps the village count; we do not always agree on the numbers.

relations.name: Simon Hollis
relations.label: trader
relations.note: He brings fish back and news with it; a fair man on the road.

relations.name: Cuthbert Stave
relations.label: friend
relations.note: A good hunter; his brother's boat went too, and he blames Edda same as me.

relations.name: Aldwyn Bexley
relations.label: debtor
relations.note: He owes me for timber; I told him plainly the debt is due at market.

relations.name: Sedge Gannet
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: A quiet man with a sharp eye; his near wreck hardened the talk against Edda.

relations.name: Tern Gannet
relations.label: fish runner
relations.note: She carries our fish to Brackenford and hates the gate-due as much as I do.

relations.name: Colm Wray
relations.label: the old woman's boy
relations.note: He trims the wick up at the light and says nothing; I have not asked him what he has seen.

relations.name: Hob Garrow
relations.label: elder of Elmwick
relations.note: He is loud about the Lakemead and was loud about the grain we could not pay; no friend to Thornby.

relations.name: Marra Brine
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She has not spoken to me since the Lean Year, and I do not know what to say to her now.

relations.name: Nerys Bexley
relations.label: debtor's wife
relations.note: A quay woman learning the fields; she trades eggs fairly and I would not press her husband in front of her.

relations.name: Pike Tarn
relations.label: hunter
relations.note: He hunts the cape with Cuthbert and they have quarrelled over the trapping ground; I want it kept quiet.

memories.gist: The Lean Year came and Brackenford lent us grain; I signed for forty baskets and thought we would pay by the next harvest.
They brought my brother up from the rocks below the north light; the boat was in pieces and the light was burning.
Perrin came to me and said he wanted to marry Inga; I thought it a good match until the talk began.
Rook Tarn read me the tally and it did not match the ledger; we argued and left it half-settled.
Aldwyn Bexley took a load of timber on credit for Hob Garrow's barn and swore to pay at the next market.

stances.why: A village that does not pay what it owes has no name worth having.
My brother drowned below her light and someone must be held to it.
Cuthbert and Pike will have each other's snares if no one speaks; I will not choose between them yet.
The talk is talk; he is a grown man and the boat is his to keep.

pastimes: mending the boat's oars and caulking on the shingle at low tide
sitting at the inn of an evening with a mug, listening to the old men's tales
walking the north shore at dusk to read the weather
Osric Dunn.calling: I am a fisherman and headman, and the sea's honesty is the only ledger I trust.

Rona Dunn.narrative: I keep the cook-fire and the smoke shed, and the village eats because I do. Osric carries the debt and I carry the worry of it. Inga works beside me and I watch her, because the women at the smoke shed have begun to talk about her and Perrin. I have said nothing to either of them, and I will not until I know my own mind.
goals: smoke enough fish to see Thornby through the winter
keep the common store from running short
decide what to say about Perrin and Inga
trade smoked fish with Simon Hollis for what we lack
learn a new cure for the smoked fish that keeps through a wet winter
see Hob grow into a steady hand
Rona Dunn.mood: watchful, warm to her own, uneasy underneath

relations.name: Osric Dunn
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He carries the debt and I carry him; that is how it has always been.

relations.name: Perrin Dunn
relations.label: son
relations.note: A good boy; I will not have the village make him ashamed of his choice.

relations.name: Inga Dunn
relations.label: niece
relations.note: She works hard at the cook-fire; I watch her and say nothing.

relations.name: Hob Dunn
relations.label: ward
relations.note: He is underfoot at the smoke shed and I would not have him elsewhere.

relations.name: Simon Hollis
relations.label: trader
relations.note: He brings fish back and takes our smoke; a fair trade and a fair word.

relations.name: Tern Gannet
relations.label: fish-road runner
relations.note: She carries our fish to Brackenford and hates the gate-due as much as we do.

relations.name: Mavis Tarn
relations.label: herb-wife
relations.note: She trades herbs and tends our sick; a good neighbour.

relations.name: Edda Wray
relations.label: accused
relations.note: Osric blames her and I keep my own counsel; the light is a hard thing to prove.

relations.name: Merrow Stave
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: We trade seeds and she keeps her plots well.

memories.gist: The Lean Year came and I stretched the common store with roots and smoked fish until the grain came from Brackenford.
Inga came to work beside me at the cook-fire and the smoke shed; she has quick hands and a quiet way.
The women at the smoke shed began to talk about Perrin and Inga being cousins, and I heard them and said nothing.
Simon Hollis came up the shore with a load of Brackenford goods and took our smoked fish back; we settled fair.

stances.why: The common store is the village's life and I keep it.
The talk is the women's, not mine to spread; I will speak when I know my mind.
We cannot pay in grain we do not have; smoked fish is what we can give.
Osric is sure and I am not; a light is a hard thing to prove wrong.

Rona Dunn.secret: I have heard the women say Inga is too close kin for Perrin, and part of me wonders if they are right.
pastimes: tending the smoke shed and the cook-fire
walking the shingle for mussels and samphire at low water
visiting Mavis Tarn for herbs and a quiet word
Rona Dunn.calling: I keep the fire and the smoke shed, and the village eats because I do.

Perrin Dunn.narrative: I fish the north shore with my father and keep the boat, and I mean to marry Inga and take her out on the water with me. I do not see what the talk is about; she is the best hand with a net in Thornby. I owe Simon Hollis for a net and I will pay him when the catch is good. The debt to Brackenford is my father's worry, but it is mine too.
goals: marry Inga and keep the boat with her
pay Simon Hollis for the net
bring in a catch good enough to help the debt
keep clear of the talk about him and Inga
own a boat of his own, not only his father's
learn the deep-water marks off the cape
Perrin Dunn.mood: eager, happy, a little puzzled by the village

relations.name: Osric Dunn
relations.label: father
relations.note: He taught me the shore and the boat; I would not shame him.

relations.name: Rona Dunn
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She keeps the fire and the smoke; she watches Inga and me and says nothing.

relations.name: Inga Dunn
relations.label: courting
relations.note: She is the best hand with a net in Thornby and I mean to marry her.

relations.name: Hob Dunn
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: He mends nets on the shingle and I let him come out when the sea is kind.

relations.name: Simon Hollis
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: I owe him for a net; he is fair and I will pay when the catch is good.

relations.name: Cuthbert Stave
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: A good hunter; he keeps the cape clear of wolves for all of us.

relations.name: Edda Wray
relations.label: accused
relations.note: My father blames her for my uncle's boat; I keep my mouth shut about it.

relations.name: Sedge Gannet
relations.label: fisher
relations.note: A quiet man with a good eye for weather, and he near wrecked last winter.

memories.gist: My father took me out on the north shore when I was small and showed me how the tide runs past the cape.
Inga came down to the shallows with her small boat and we raced the tide in; I knew then I wanted her.
Simon Hollis left me a net on credit and said to pay when the catch was good; I have not paid yet.
The village began to talk about Inga and me being cousins by marriage, and I do not see what the talk is about.

stances.why: She is the best hand with a net in Thornby and the boat is ours to keep.
Simon Hollis trusted me with a net and I will not have him think me a bad debtor.
My father carries it, but the catch I bring in is Thornby's and the ledger is Thornby's.
The village will say what it says; I will not let it turn me from Inga.

pastimes: fishing the north shore from the boat
mending and tarring nets on the shingle
dicing at the inn with Sedge Gannet and the other young fishers
Perrin Dunn.calling: I fish the north shore and keep the boat, and I mean to make my living from the water.

Inga Dunn.narrative: I fish the shallows from my small boat and mend the village nets, and I work beside Rona at the cook-fire. Perrin wants to marry me and I want him, but the women at the smoke shed have begun to talk about us being cousins, and I have not told him what they say. I think Edda Wray should be watched; a light that fails once can fail again. I keep my own counsel and my own boat.
goals: decide what to do about the talk and Perrin
keep her small boat and her share of the catch
mend the village nets well enough to be thanked for it
see that someone watches Edda's light
save enough marks to buy better net-twine and a second oar
learn the herb-wife's salves for rope-burn and cold hands
Inga Dunn.mood: warm, watchful, a little stung by the talk

relations.name: Perrin Dunn
relations.label: courting
relations.note: He wants me and I want him, and I have not told him what the women say.

relations.name: Osric Dunn
relations.label: uncle
relations.note: He is fond of me and has not thought about the match at all, I think.

relations.name: Rona Dunn
relations.label: aunt
relations.note: She watches me at the cook-fire and says nothing; I do not know what she thinks.

relations.name: Hob Dunn
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: He is a quiet lad and good with a net; I let him help me mend.

relations.name: Edda Wray
relations.label: watched
relations.note: A light that fails once can fail again; she should be watched.

relations.name: Mavis Tarn
relations.label: herb-wife
relations.note: She tends the village sick and trades herbs; a good woman to know.

relations.name: Wren Stave
relations.label: neighbour's child
relations.note: She follows her father to the cape and is afraid of the light; I do not blame her.

relations.name: Rook Tarn
relations.label: elder
relations.note: He keeps the tally and the nets, and he is fair.

relations.name: Tern Gannet
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She runs the fish road and hates the gate-due, and I do not blame her.

memories.gist: My uncle Osric gave me a small boat when I came to the Dunn house, and I have fished the shallows from it since.
Perrin and I raced the tide in from the shallows and he said he wanted me; I said I wanted him too.
The women at the smoke shed began to say Perrin and I are too close kin, and I heard them and said nothing.
I mended the village nets through a long afternoon with Hob Dunn handing me the twine.

stances.why: I want him, but I will not have the village say I brought shame on the Dunn house.
The shallows are mine and the small boat is mine; I will not be beholden.
A light that fails once can fail again, and boats go on the rocks below it.
The village nets are the village's catch, and my hands are good at it.

Inga Dunn.secret: I have heard the women say Perrin and I are too close kin, and I have not told him.
pastimes: fishing the shallows from her small boat
sitting with Mavis Tarn while she works her herbs
Inga Dunn.calling: I fish the shallows and mend nets, and I want a boat and a catch that are my own.

Hob Dunn.narrative: I live in the Dunn house and mend nets on the shingle. Perrin lets me come out in the boat when the sea is kind. I play with Wren Stave when the Stave folk come down the shore. I do not like the dark stair at the light and I do not like the wolves.
goals: mend a net clean through without a knot slipping
go out in the boat with Perrin again
play with Wren Stave
mend a whole net clean through without a knot slipping
learn to row the small boat alone
Hob Dunn.mood: quiet, content, a little wary of the dark

relations.name: Osric Dunn
relations.label: guardian
relations.note: He took me in and gives me bread; I mend nets to earn it.

relations.name: Rona Dunn
relations.label: guardian
relations.note: She keeps the fire and lets me sit by it; she is kind to me.

relations.name: Perrin Dunn
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: He lets me come out in the boat when the sea is kind.

relations.name: Inga Dunn
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She lets me hand her the twine when she mends the nets.

relations.name: Wren Stave
relations.label: playmate
relations.note: She comes down the shore and we play on the shingle.

memories.gist: Perrin took me out in the boat and I held the rope while he pulled the net in.
I sat by Rona's cook-fire and she gave me bread and told me to stay out of the smoke.
Wren Stave and I played on the shingle until the tide came up.

pastimes: playing on the shingle with Wren Stave
watching the boats come in and counting the catch
Hob Dunn.calling: I want to be a fisherman like Perrin and go out in the boat.
